name: נגזרת של e^t/(t·ln t) – מנה (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Find the following derivative:

\( \displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left( {{CT:1}}\right) = \) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Use the quotient rule; the derivative of the denominator needs the product rule.
Step 1 — The quotient rule
To solve this problem you will need to use the product rule and the quotient rule.
The product rule: \( \frac{d}{dx}(uv)=u'v+uv' \)
The quotient rule: \( \frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{u}{v}\right)=\frac{u'v-uv'}{v^2} \)
Let \(f({{CT:0}})={{CT:2}}\) and \(g({{CT:0}})={{CT:3}}\). Then,

\[ \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:1}}\right] = \frac{\frac{df}{d{{CT:0}}}\cdot g - f\cdot \frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}}}{g^2}. \]

Step 2 — The denominator: the product rule
In order to calculate \(\frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}}\) you need to use the product rule, by defining two new functions: \(h({{CT:0}})={{CT:0}}\) and \(i({{CT:0}})={{CT:4}}\) so that \(g({{CT:0}})=h({{CT:0}})i({{CT:0}})\). So,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[{{CT:3}}] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{dh}{d{{CT:0}}}\cdot i + h\cdot \frac{di}{d{{CT:0}}}\\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle [{{CT:5}}]{{CT:4}} + {{CT:0}}[{{CT:6}}] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:7}} \end{array} \]

Step 3 — Putting it together
Hence,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:1}}\right] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{\frac{df}{d{{CT:0}}}\cdot g - f\cdot \frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}}}{g^2} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{[{{CT:8}}]{{CT:3}} - {{CT:2}}[{{CT:7}}]}{[{{CT:3}}]^2} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{{{CT:9}} - {{CT:10}}}{{{CT:11}}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:12}} \end{array} \]
